title: Readout-Induced Leakage in Superconducting Circuits with Nonlinear Couplings
authors: Sumeru Hazra, Wei Dai, Daniel K. Weiss, Pranav D. Parakh, Luigi Frunzio, Michel H. Devoret
abstract: In superconducting circuits, drive-induced unwanted transitions limit the readout power, thereby constraining readout speed and fidelity. When such transitions excite the qubit into leakage states, they produce correlated errors that are particularly harmful for quantum error correction. Native nonlinear qubit-readout resonator coupling is a promising alternative to conventional linear hybridization because it provides intrinsic Purcell protection and stricter selection rules for multiphoton processes. In realistic devices, however, we show that such a coupling alone neither eliminates nor necessarily suppresses drive-induced transitions. Instead, if not appropriately engineered, these couplings often worsen the situation by introducing additional parasitic processes. Moreover, the rates of these unwanted transitions remain sensitive to the choice of readout frequency, regardless of the coupling mechanism. We demonstrate that readout-induced leakage can thus vary by orders of magnitude even when readout frequencies differ by less than ~7%. Our results establish that the benefits of native nonlinear couplings are realized only through informed device design, including the spectral placement of relevant auxiliary modes and elimination of parasitic ones.
summary: This research investigates how drive-induced leakage limits readout performance in superconducting qubits. By comparing linear versus nonlinear coupling schemes, the authors demonstrate that while nonlinearity is promising, its benefit critically depends on precise device design to avoid parasitic resonance pathways. The work establishes that frequency dependence is paramount, requiring comprehensive spectral characterization for reliable quantum computing operation.
main_problem: Drive-induced unwanted transitions (leakage) limit the readout power and fidelity of superconducting qubits, posing a significant challenge for quantum error correction.
main_result: Leakage is highly sensitive to the choice of readout frequency, demonstrating that nonlinear couplings only provide benefits through careful, informed device engineering rather than inherently suppressing all leakage pathways.
method: The study employs both theoretical Floquet steady-state simulations and detailed experimental measurements (e.g., correlation decay analysis) to characterize multi-photon resonance landscapes.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting qubits coupled to readout resonators, analyzed using various nonlinear coupling schemes like native cosine-cosine or mediated couplings involving auxiliary modes.
key_observables: Readout fidelity ($F_{ge}$), leakage probability ($\mathcal{L}_\uparrow$), seepage rate ($\mathcal{L}_\downarrow$), and the multi-photon resonance landscape ($\Theta$ vs. frequency/power).
important_parameters: Readout drive frequency ($\omega_d/\omega_q$) and readout power (related to steady-state photon number $ ar{n}_r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximations, such as assuming an incoherent leakage model or neglecting quantum fluctuations of the resonator in certain theoretical derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate resonance landscapes showing how different couplings affect multiphoton resonances; experimental data show correlation decay curves and measured fidelity values across varying readout parameters.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares various coupling Hamiltonians (linear vs. nonlinear), analyzes the resulting multi-photon resonance spectra via Floquet theory, and validates these findings with detailed measurements of readout fidelity and leakage rates as a function of drive frequency.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial experimental and theoretical benchmarks for mitigating decoherence sources in superconducting quantum processors by mapping out the complex parameter space where unwanted coupling channels become active.
